text: Fourier coefficients can be computed independently by projection because the basis functions {1, cos(nx), sin(nx)} are:
choices: mutually orthogonal under the L^2 inner product (integral of the product over a period)
explanation: Orthogonality (the integral over a period of the product of distinct basis functions is zero) lets each coefficient be found separately as a projection. The basis functions are not normalized (cos(nx) has norm sqrt(pi) on [-pi, pi]), and they are eigenfunctions of the second-derivative operator, not of multiplication by x.
